newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Lower House passes central bank reforms.
newsitem.headline: Japan Lower House passes central bank reforms.

text.p: Japan's Lower House of parliament passed a bill on Thursday revising central bank laws to give the Bank of Japan (BOJ) more independence from the government in setting monetary policy, parliament officials said.

The Lower House also passed resolutions calling for a sweeping reorganisation of the central bank, including the consolidation of branches and other offices and the disposal of unnecessary assets. The resolutions also called upon the central bank to review BOJ officials' incomes, which have been criticised as being too high, they said.

The bill has been sent to the Upper House of parliament for debate and is expected to be passed during the current parliamentary session, which ends on June 18. The revisions are to be enacted from April 1998, they said.

The BOJ law revision, the first in over 50 years, is part of a deregulation drive promoted by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto. The revision aims to strengthen the BOJ's policy-making board and to boost the transparency of decision-making processes.
